> Complete NVGEMM epilogue matching and code generation across dense and block-scaled providers. Support wide and local reductions, auxiliary and feed-main forms, shared and chained consumers, transposed and dynamic layouts, and heterogeneous tuple outputs while retaining validated fallbacks for unsupported graph shapes.
>
> Extract backend-neutral FX dependency analysis and output planning from FlexGEMM into shared GEMM epilogue infrastructure. NVGEMM analyzes existing Inductor loop IR without reconstructing FX, then both paths converge on the same typed reduction geometry, expression, plan, argument ABI, and CuTeDSL provider machinery.
>
> Test Plan:
>
> ```bash
> lintrunner -a
> ```
>
> Authored with an AI assistant.

items.body:
<!-- ai-review-bot -->
## AI-Review

> *Automated multi-agent review (2 Claude + 2 Codex + synthesis). This is AI-generated — please verify findings manually.*

---

## Critical Issues (must fix)

- **Restore a single, explicit decode boundary for operator args.** Removing `from_operator_args` deletes the one place that translated the loosely-typed operator-arg namespace (`local_reduce_*`) into the typed `GemmReductionArguments`. This is only a win if construction now happens explicitly in *one* location; if callers build the struct inline at multiple sites, the decode logic scatters and drifts. Confirm the single construction boundary exists (it can live outside this class), and verify every call site was switched from reading the raw operator-args object to reading a `GemmReductionArguments` instance — otherwise `getattr(args, "group", ...)` on the old object silently falls back to defaults and produces a wrong specialization key. *(Consensus: both design reviewers + Claude bug review; Codex Design = Request Changes.)*

- **Don't let all-defaults make an incomplete `GemmReductionArguments` silently valid.** With every field defaulted, a genuinely-enabled-but-mis-wired instance is indistinguishable from the "disabled" sentinel at construction time — validity is only checked later via `enabled`, so wiring failures masquerade as "no reduction." Introduce a dedicated `disabled()` factory for the sentinel and require the specialization fields on enabled instances (or split into distinct disabled/enabled variants with construction-time validation). *(Consensus: both design reviewers; Codex Design = Request Changes.)*

## Important Suggestions (should fix)

- **Type `secondary_feed_type` symmetrically with `reduction_type`.** The primary `reduction_type` gets first-class parsing via `GemmReductionDescriptor.parse` / the `.descriptor` property, but `secondary_feed_type` stays a bare `str` with no typed accessor. If they're the same category of thing, give them the same abstraction; the asymmetry invites ad hoc string parsing at the secondary call sites. *(Claude design review.)*

## Minor Notes (consider)

- **Consolidate the repeated field quartet.** `group`, `axis`, `reduction_type`, `source_type` (plus `feeds_main`, `secondary_feed_*`) are duplicated across `Config`/`Plan`/`Arguments`. The layering justifies separate types, but a small embedded value object for the shared core would keep the layers in sync as fields evolve. *(Claude design review.)*

- **Reconsider the `gemm_epilogue_utils` home for generic helpers.** The moved `statically_known*` helpers are generic sizevar/symbolic-shape utilities, not GEMM-specific. A GEMM-scoped `*_utils` module will accrete unrelated helpers; if these are reusable, a shared symbolic-shape location is a better home. *(Claude design review.)*

---

**Note on scope:** Both bug reviewers found no confirmed bugs; the renames (`GemmReductionExpression -> GemmReductionDescriptor`, `.expression -> .descriptor`, `SPECIALIZATION_KEYS -> SPECIALIZATION_FIELDS` with rekeyed values) are internally consistent within the diff. The only bug-level risk is the call-site verification folded into Critical item 1 — worth a direct check since the surrounding module/callers weren't available to the reviewers.
